1. use crate::hal::mem::spec_page_size;
2. 
3. verus! {
4. 
5. //==================================================================================================
6. // Abstract state of the kernel identity map
7. //==================================================================================================
8. 
9. /// Abstract state of the kernel identity map (see `view_design.md`).
10. ///
11. /// This is a ghost model of *global* state: the in-scope functions are free functions backed by
12. /// the `KERNEL_PD_PADDR` / `KERNEL_CR3` atomics plus a BSS page-table pool, so there is no owning
13. /// exec struct. Addresses use `int` (the `View` of `PhysicalAddress` / `PageAligned`), consistent
14. /// with the sibling `mm::phys` abstraction (`FrameAllocView` keys frames by `int`).
15. pub ghost struct IdentityMapView {
16.     /// Whether the lazy identity mapper has been initialized (i.e. `init` has published the kernel
17.     /// page directory). Before initialization the boot page tables are still active and every
18.     /// `identity_map_page` is a successful no-op, so this flag selects which transition applies.
19.     pub initialized: bool,
20. 
21.     /// The set of identity-mapped pages, each identified by its page-aligned physical base
22.     /// address. Membership means: the page is **present, writable, supervisor-only**, and
23.     /// reachable at its own physical address in the kernel address space. Permissions are uniform
24.     /// across all mapped pages, so they are encoded by membership rather than stored per page.
25.     pub mapped: Set<int>,
26. }
27. 
28. /// Current abstract state of the global kernel identity map.
29. ///
30. /// Uninterpreted accessor: the identity-map state lives in module-level singletons
31. /// (`KERNEL_PD_PADDR` / `KERNEL_CR3` and the BSS page-table pool) whose value is not directly
32. /// spec-readable. The cross-call transition (`v -> v'`) is realized in the proving phase by a
33. /// ghost token over those singletons; during the specification phase it is read like `self@`.
34. /// This mirrors `mm::phys::phys_view()` -- the same singleton-global boundary, not a verification
35. /// escape.
36. pub uninterp spec fn identity_map_view() -> IdentityMapView;
37. 
38. //==================================================================================================
39. // Page-address vocabulary
40. //==================================================================================================
41. 
42. /// An address is page-aligned when it is a multiple of the page size.
43. pub open spec fn spec_is_page_aligned(addr: int) -> bool {
44.     addr % spec_page_size() == 0
45. }
46. 
47. /// The page-aligned base address of the page containing `addr`.
48. pub open spec fn spec_page_base(addr: int) -> int {
49.     addr - (addr % spec_page_size())
50. }
51. 
52. //==================================================================================================
53. // Invariants and queries
54. //==================================================================================================
55. 
56. impl IdentityMapView {
57.     /// Implementation-consistency invariant (e.g. the abstract `mapped` set agrees with the
58.     /// present PDE/PTE bits and the page-table-pool bounds). Placeholder during specification;
59.     /// the proving phase fills it in once the concrete `view()` body is realized.
60.     pub open spec fn internal_inv(self) -> bool {
61.         true
62.     }
63. 
64.     /// Well-formedness invariant callers rely on.
65.     pub open spec fn inv(self) -> bool {
66.         &&& self.internal_inv()
67.         // Every recorded page is identified by a page-aligned base address.
68.         &&& (forall|p: int| #[trigger] self.mapped.contains(p) ==> spec_is_page_aligned(p))
69.         // Before initialization no lazy mapping has been installed; coverage is provided entirely
70.         // by the boot page tables.
71.         &&& (!self.initialized ==> self.mapped =~= Set::empty())
72.     }
73. 
74.     /// The page based at `page` is reachable at its own physical address right now. Before init the
75.     /// boot tables make every page reachable; after init reachability is exactly membership in
76.     /// `mapped`. This is the headline resource callers obtain from `identity_map_page` on `Ok`.
77.     pub open spec fn accessible(self, page: int) -> bool {
78.         !self.initialized || self.mapped.contains(page)
79.     }
80. 
81.     /// Unconditional install of one page (idempotent). Models the leaf step `ensure_pte` realizes:
82.     /// it always adds the page to the map.
83.     pub open spec fn spec_install_page(self, page: int) -> IdentityMapView {
84.         IdentityMapView { mapped: self.mapped.insert(page), ..self }
85.     }
86. 
87.     /// Full effect of `identity_map_page`: install the page when the mapper is initialized,
88.     /// otherwise a no-op (boot tables already cover it). Either way the page ends up `accessible`.
89.     pub open spec fn spec_map_page(self, page: int) -> IdentityMapView {
90.         if self.initialized {
91.             self.spec_install_page(page)
92.         } else {
93.             self
94.         }
95.     }
96. }
97. 
98. //==================================================================================================
99. // Dependency contracts for not-yet-verified modules
100. //
101. // The kernel HAL paging layer (`arch::mem::paging` types/functions) and the kernel
102. // `page_table_allocator` storage marker are not verified yet. They are registered as external
103. // types / given trusted external specifications here so that the in-scope identity-map bodies can
104. // be translated. These are placeholders: when the underlying modules are verified, their real
105. // `#[verus_spec]` contracts supersede them. The intra-call obligations they would discharge are
106. // currently `admit()`-ed in the exec bodies, so minimal (state-free) contracts suffice.
107. //==================================================================================================
108. 
109. use super::page_table_allocator::PageTableBss;
110. 
111. // NOTE: `TableEntry` (trait), `Table<E>`, `TableIndex`, `pd_index`, `pt_index`,
112. // `Table::from_address`, `Table::read`, and `Table::write` now have real
113. // `#[verus_spec]`/`#[verus_verify]` contracts in `arch::x86::mem::paging::table`.

1. // Copyright(c) The Maintainers of Nanvix.
2. // Licensed under the MIT License.
3. 
4. // FixedSizeBumpAllocator - Specifications
5. //
6. // This file contains the abstract View (`BumpView`), its invariant and geometry
7. // helpers, the numeric specification of `align_up`, and the proof-lemma targets
8. // that encode the caller expectations. See
9. // `verus-ai-logs/nanvix-phys-bump-allocator/view_design.md` for the design
10. // rationale.
11. //
12. // NOTE: Attaching `BumpView` as the `View` of `FixedSizeBumpAllocator` is a later
13. // phase (view_design.md, end of section 2). It requires an atomic-ghost / PointsTo
14. // token to model the interior-mutable `AtomicUsize` cursor, because the raw atomic
15. // value is not readable in spec (vstd: "NO support for reasoning about the values
16. // inside the atomics"). Until then `BumpView` is referenced by the proof lemmas in
17. // `lib.proof.rs`, which state the caller-facing guarantees over the abstract pool.
18. 
19. verus! {
20. 
21. //==================================================================================================
22. // std-library specifications not yet covered by vstd
23. //==================================================================================================
24. 
25. // `usize::div_ceil` rounds the quotient towards positive infinity. It panics on a
26. // zero divisor, hence the `y != 0` precondition. For unsigned operands the result
27. // never overflows, and equals `ceil(x / y) == (x + y - 1) / y`.
28. pub assume_specification [ <usize>::div_ceil ](x: usize, y: usize) -> (result: usize)
29.     requires
30.         y != 0,
31.     ensures
32.         result as int == (x as int + y as int - 1) / (y as int),
33. ;
34. 
35. //==================================================================================================
36. // align_up - numeric specification
37. //==================================================================================================
38. 
39. /// Ghost constant: the stable base address revealed by a backend `S`'s
40. /// `as_mut_ptr()`. Uninterpreted because a static's address is opaque to Verus.
41. pub uninterp spec fn base_of<S: ?Sized>() -> int;
42. 
43. /// Abstract address of a freshly handed-out slot reference.
44. ///
45. /// Uninterpreted: a Verus `&mut T` reference carries no spec-readable address
46. /// (only raw pointers expose `.addr()`), so — mirroring `raw-array`'s uninterpreted
47. /// `view(&self) -> Seq<T>` — the address a caller observes for a returned slot is
48. /// modeled abstractly. `alloc`/`alloc_as` assert their alignment and in-bounds
49. /// guarantees over `slot_ref_addr(slot)`.
50. pub uninterp spec fn slot_ref_addr<T: ?Sized>(r: &T) -> int;
51. 
52. /// Least multiple of `alignment` that is `>= value`; `None` when `alignment == 0`
53. /// or when that multiple does not fit in a `usize`.
54. ///
55. /// This is the View-independent numeric meaning of `align_up`. The allocator's
56. /// `stride` (see `BumpView::inv`) is pinned to this function.
57. pub open spec fn align_up_spec(value: nat, alignment: nat) -> Option<nat> {
58.     if alignment == 0 {
59.         None
60.     } else {
61.         let m: int = ((value + alignment - 1) / (alignment as int)) * (alignment as int);
62.         if m > usize::MAX as int {
63.             None
64.         } else {
65.             Some(m as nat)
66.         }
67.     }
68. }
69. 
70. //==================================================================================================
71. // BumpView - abstract pool model
72. //==================================================================================================
73. 
74. /// Abstract view of a `FixedSizeBumpAllocator<N, A, S>`.
75. ///
76. /// Pure ghost description of the slot pool: no atomics, no raw pointers, no cursor
77. /// mechanism. Carries the fixed pool geometry plus the single dynamic quantity
78. /// `allocated` (the number of slots handed out so far).
79. #[verifier::ext_equal]
80. pub struct BumpView {
81.     /// Base address of the backing region (`S::as_mut_ptr()` as an integer).
82.     pub base: int,
83.     /// Distance in bytes between consecutive slots (`align_up(unit_size, unit_align)`).
84.     pub stride: nat,
85.     /// Size of each slot in bytes (the const generic `N`).
86.     pub unit_size: nat,
87.     /// Required alignment of each slot in bytes (the const generic `A`).
88.     pub unit_align: nat,
89.     /// Number of slots the pool can ever yield (`S::NUM_UNITS`).
90.     pub capacity: nat,
91.     /// Total size in bytes of the backing region (`S::STORAGE_SIZE`).
92.     pub storage_size: nat,
93.     /// Number of slots already handed out. The only dynamic field.
94.     pub allocated: nat,
95. }
96. 
97. impl BumpView {
98.     /// Address of slot `i` (0-based). The pool's geometry, independent of the
99.     /// allocation mechanism.
100.     pub open spec fn slot_addr(self, i: int) -> int {
101.         self.base + i * (self.stride as int)
102.     }
103. 
104.     /// A slot index is *consumed* iff it is below the high-water mark.
105.     pub open spec fn is_consumed(self, i: int) -> bool {
106.         0 <= i < self.allocated
107.     }
108. 
109.     /// The allocator still has at least one free slot.
110.     pub open spec fn has_capacity(self) -> bool {
111.         self.allocated < self.capacity
112.     }
113. 
114.     /// Well-formedness of the abstract pool. Each clause backs a caller-visible
115.     /// guarantee (see `view_design.md` section 3).
116.     pub open spec fn inv(self) -> bool {
117.         // (a) Geometry is well formed: non-empty, non-overlapping slots.
118.         &&& self.unit_size > 0
119.         &&& self.unit_align > 0
120.         &&& self.stride >= self.unit_size
121.         // (b) Stride is the up-alignment of the unit size to the unit alignment,
122.         //     and every slot start inherits `unit_align` from an aligned base.
123.         &&& align_up_spec(self.unit_size, self.unit_align) == Some(self.stride)
124.         &&& (self.stride as int) % (self.unit_align as int) == 0
125.         &&& self.base % (self.unit_align as int) == 0
126.         // (c) The pool fits inside the backing region.
127.         &&& (self.capacity as int) * (self.stride as int) <= self.storage_size as int
128.         // (d) Addresses do not wrap the usize space.
129.         &&& self.base >= 0
130.         &&& self.base + (self.storage_size as int) <= usize::MAX as int + 1
131.         // (e) Monotone-capacity ceiling.
132.         &&& self.allocated <= self.capacity
133.     }
134. 
135.     /// The three geometric guarantees the kernel's `unsafe` soundness relies on,
136.     /// stated over the whole pool: every slot is aligned, in-bounds, and distinct.
137.     pub open spec fn geometry_ok(self) -> bool {
138.         &&& (forall|i: int|
139.             0 <= i < self.capacity ==> #[trigger] self.slot_addr(i) % (self.unit_align as int) == 0)
140.         &&& (forall|i: int|
141.             0 <= i < self.capacity ==> {
142.                 &&& self.base <= #[trigger] self.slot_addr(i)
143.                 &&& self.slot_addr(i) + (self.unit_size as int) <= self.base + (self.storage_size
144.                     as int)
145.             })
146.         &&& (forall|i: int, j: int|
147.             (0 <= i < self.capacity && 0 <= j < self.capacity && i != j)
148.                 ==> (#[trigger] self.slot_addr(i)) != (#[trigger] self.slot_addr(j)))
149.     }
150. 
151.     /// Abstract transition performed by a successful allocation: one more slot is
152.     /// consumed, nothing else changes.
153.     pub open spec fn spec_alloc(self) -> BumpView {
154.         BumpView { allocated: (self.allocated + 1) as nat, ..self }
155.     }
156. }
157. 
158. //==================================================================================================
159. // FixedSizeBumpAllocator - view accessor
160. //==================================================================================================
161. 
162. /// Abstract view of the allocator's slot pool.
163. ///
164. /// Uninterpreted (mirrors `raw-array`'s `impl View for RawArray`): the dynamic
165. /// `allocated` field abstracts the interior-mutable `AtomicUsize` cursor, whose
166. /// value is not spec-readable. `inv()` pins `base/stride/unit_size/unit_align/
167. /// capacity/storage_size` to the type-level constants. The `v -> v'` transition
168. /// (cross-call uniqueness, `allocated + 1`) needs a ghost token and is deferred
169. /// to the proving phase (see `lemma_alloc_transition`, view_design.md section 7).
170. ///
171. /// A free `uninterp spec fn` is used rather than an `impl View`/inherent `spec fn
172. /// view`, because adding a second `impl` block (trait or inherent) on
173. /// `FixedSizeBumpAllocator` alongside the exec method block collides during Verus
174. /// front-end lowering of this crate (`include!`-composed spec/proof modules) and
175. /// triggers a duplicate-impl-path panic (`vir/src/context.rs`). Callers read the
176. /// view via `bump_view(self)` exactly as they would `self.view()`.
177. pub uninterp spec fn bump_view<const N: usize, const A: usize, S: BssStorage>(
178.     a: &FixedSizeBumpAllocator<N, A, S>,
179. ) -> BumpView;
180. 
181. } // verus!
182.

# Verification TODO — `mm::virt::identity_map` (cheating-elimination pass)

Honest hand-off of genuinely-stuck proof obligations per the `verus-constraints`
escalation ladder. These are **not** accepted trust assumptions and **not** code
bugs. They are the cross-module *proving-phase ghost-token* obligations the whole
bottom-up effort defers (the same state every sibling `mm::phys::*` singleton free
function is in).

The 3 in-scope exec functions (`ensure_pt`, `ensure_pte`, `identity_map_page`)
retain `proof! { admit(); }`. Every obligation below was reproduced empirically in
this pass by deleting the `admit()` and running
`make verify-kernel MODULE=mm::virt::identity_map`
(result: `6 verified, 3 errors`, exit 101). The exec code is byte-identical to
`verus-ai-prove-bottom-up` except for those 3 ghost `admit()` lines.

## Root cause (shared by all 3 entries) — a logical impossibility, not a missing lemma

`identity_map_view()` is declared `uninterp spec fn identity_map_view() -> IdentityMapView`
(`identity_map.spec.rs:36`). With **no parameters** it denotes one fixed-but-opaque
constant value `V`; `requires` only tells the verifier `V.inv()`. Its connection to
the concrete singleton state (`KERNEL_PD_PADDR`/`KERNEL_CR3` + the BSS page-table
pool) is — by the file's own design comments — "realized in the proving phase by a
ghost token over those singletons." That framework does not exist in the codebase.

Two of the three functions carry **result-dependent, opposite** postconditions over
this constant:

- `ensure_pte`: `Ok => V.mapped.contains(p)` **and** `Err => !V.mapped.contains(p)`.
- `identity_map_page`: `Ok => V.accessible(p)` **and** `Err => !V.accessible(p)`.

For a single fixed unknown `V`, exactly one of `contains(p)` / `!contains(p)` is true,
but the exec **return decision** (PTE read success, frame-number range, `pd_paddr==0`
init test) is not tied to that fixed set. Therefore **no proof, lemma, or `vstd`
search can discharge both branches** — it is logically impossible while the view is a
parameterless constant. Confirmed empirically (postcondition errors at
`identity_map.rs:618` and `identity_map.rs:706`).

Eliminating the admits soundly requires making the view depend on runtime singleton
state via a ghost token. Every realization of that token is **out of scope / forbidden**
by this task's hard rules:

1. Spec-readable atomics would require replacing `core::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize`
   with a `vstd` atomic-ghost / `PointsTo` type — an exec **type/signature change** to
